AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES — END MOUNTINGS 
OF SHOCK ABSORBERS — DIMENSIONS 

AND TESTS

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

December \9%9 Price Group 4 



Automotive Vehicles Suspension and Steering Systems Sectional Committee, EDC 105 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 4 March 1 989, after the draft 
finalized by the Automotive Vehicles Suspension and Steering System Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

Shock absorbers play an important role not only for the comfort of the riders of the vehicle but also 
in the performance and life of the vehicle. End mountings for shock absorbers hold the shock absorbers 
with the vehicle in the manner required. Improper mountings or their improper placement or fitting with 
the vehicle may lead to the premature failure of the shock absorbers. 



IS 12648 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES — END MOUNTINGS 
OF SHOCK ABSORBERS - DIMENSIONS 

AND TESTS 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the shapes dimensions and 
tests of end mountings of shock absorbers for 
automobiles. 

2 SHAPES AND TYPES 

2.1 Shapes of shock absorber ends are shown in 
Fig. 1. The end mountings shall be of eyering type 
with tapered or straight bushes and stud types. 

3 DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The recommended dimensions of E 10 type eye- 
rings are given in Table 1. 

3.2 The recommended dimensions of E 20 type 
eyerings are given in Table 2. 



3.3 The recommended dimensions of S type studs 
are given in Tables 3 and 4. 

4 ALIGNMENT TOLERANCES OF ASSEMBLIES 

4.1 The alignment tolerances for lower mountings 
with eye ringsand studs shall be as given in Fig. 2. 

4.2 The dimensional alignment tolerance for upper 
mountings with eyerings and studs shall be as given 
in Fig. 3. 

5 STRENGTH REQUIREMENT 

5.1 All mountings with eyerings shall have a 
minimum pull strength and minimum impact strength 
as given in Tables 5 and 6. 

5.2 All mountings with studs shall have a minimum 
pull strength and minimum impact strength as given 
in Table 7.

6 PROCEDURE FOR CHECKING STRENGTHS 

6.1 Tensile Strength 

The tensile strength shall be checked on a universal 
tensile testing machine. The ends shall be pulled at 
a rate of 50 mm per min. 

6.2 Impact Strength 

6.2.1 The impact strength shall be checked on a 
dead weight drop testing machine. 



6.2.2 The impact strength shall be checked at the 
sub-assembly stage. 

6.2.3 The mounting shall be held in suitable fixtures 
and a dead mass of 250 N ( 25*48 kg) shall be 
dropped as shown in Fig, 4 and 5, 

6.2.4 Criterion of Passing 

The mountings shall not be separated. They may 
however bend.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards
